review_notes: I read all 415 lines of Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Asymptotics.lean and all 41 declarations in it. To test for vacuity/misleading statements I inspected the relevant pointwise and library facts: `Real.rpow_def_of_nonpos`, `Real.zero_rpow`, `Real.rpow_def_of_neg`, `Real.abs_rpow_le_abs_rpow`, `Real.rpow_le_rpow_of_exponent_ge` / `..._of_imp` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Real.lean), `Real.norm_cpow_le` / `norm_cpow_of_imp` (same file lines 316–327), `Real.isTheta_exp_comp_one` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Exp.lean:457), and the downstream consumers (Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/ContDiffHolder/Pointwise.lean:69,102; Mathlib/Computability/AkraBazzi/SumTransform.lean:506,512; Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/Injectivity.lean:107; Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/CompareExp.lean:148; Mathlib/Analysis/MellinTransform.lean:294,305). Checks performed: (1) satisfiability of every hypothesis set — all are consistent; (2) necessity of the side conditions in the base-comparison lemmas — `-1 < b` in `tendsto_rpow_atTop_of_base_lt_one` is essential (b = -2 gives `exp(x log 2) * cos (x*pi)`, unbounded; b = -1 gives `cos (x*pi)`, no limit), and `0 < b` in `tendsto_rpow_atBot_of_base_lt_one` is essential (b = 0 is eventually 0, not atTop); (3) the documented exception in `IsBigO.rpow_rpow_nhdsGE_zero_of_le_of_imp` — I verified it is genuine and not an artifact: `𝓝[≥] 0` contains the point 0, where `‖(0 : ℝ) ^ 0‖ = 1` while `‖(0 : ℝ) ^ a‖ = 0` for a ≠ 0, so no constant bound can hold eventually when b = 0, a ≠ 0; (4) degenerate exponent cases r = 0, s = 0, k = 0 and negative exponents are all handled correctly and non-trivially (e.g. IsTheta.rpow/IsBigOWith.rpow with r = 0 give the (true) 1 =Θ 1 statement, while the side conditions `0 ≤ᶠ g`, `0 ≤ r` are genuinely needed, e.g. f = 1, g = -1, r = 1/2); (5) direction of every `=O`/`=o`/`=Θ` and every filter (atTop/atBot/𝓝[>] 0/𝓝[<] 0) against its docstring — all match. I found no vacuous conclusion, no empty domain, and no statement that contradicts its documentation. Two minor, non-rubric documentation observations (not reported as findings because the mathematical claims are correct and fully expressed): the docstring of `isLittleO_exp_neg_mul_rpow_atTop` (line 337) names the exponent `s` while the binder is `b`, and `tendsto_rpow_atTop_of_base_lt_one` has no docstring mentioning the essential `-1 < b` condition (note the ENNReal analogue in Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/ENNRealLogExp.lean:143 needs only `b < 1`). Remaining uncertainty: I could not run Lean, so claims about unproved alternative formulations were avoided; all reasoning about values at the point 0 and about negative bases was done from the source definitions quoted above.
